collector.issue.permission.description: Auditex could not read the requested Microsoft 365 surface with the supplied identity.
collector.issue.permission.impact: The report has a confirmed evidence gap for this area, so the related control cannot be asserted from this run.
collector.issue.permission.remediation: Rerun with the minimum read permission required for the blocked surface, or exclude that surface from the agreed scope.
collector.issue.permission.expected_value: The collector can read the requested surface.

collector.issue.service.description: The collector reached a tenant surface that is absent, disabled, not provisioned, or temporarily unavailable.
collector.issue.service.impact: Evidence for the affected service remains partial until the tenant state or service availability changes.
collector.issue.service.remediation: Confirm licensing and service availability, then rerun only the affected collector where appropriate.
collector.issue.service.expected_value: The target service surface responds successfully.

collector.issue.collector.description: A collector finished with an operational error unrelated to normal permission or service-state handling.
collector.issue.collector.impact: The affected evidence set may be missing, incomplete, or unsuitable for comparison.
collector.issue.collector.remediation: Inspect the collector diagnostic row, fix the runtime or input condition, and rerun the collector.
collector.issue.collector.expected_value: The collector completes without runtime errors.

coverage.gap.description: One or more audit surfaces are blocked or partial, limiting assurance for that provider area.
coverage.gap.impact: Important risks can remain unknown when required collectors cannot read the surface or only return partial evidence.
coverage.gap.remediation: Resolve the affected collector permissions, scopes, service availability, or configuration, then rerun the audit.
coverage.gap.expected_value: All in-scope audit surfaces complete successfully or have an accepted scope decision.

reports_usage.concealed_names.description: The tenant report setting displayConcealedNames is enabled, so Microsoft 365 usage reports show hashed user, group, and site names.
reports_usage.concealed_names.impact: Per-user usage evidence in this run cannot be tied to named identities; usage-based conclusions are limited to aggregate counts.
reports_usage.concealed_names.remediation: No security change is required; concealed names protect privacy. If named per-user evidence is in scope, a report administrator can temporarily disable concealed names in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Settings > Org settings > Reports) under an approved change, then re-enable it.
references: Microsoft 365 admin center report privacy settings
reports_usage.concealed_names.expected_value: Report privacy setting is known and accounted for in the audit scope.

sharepoint.broad_link.description: SharePoint or OneDrive evidence indicates a sharing link with broad audience reach.
sharepoint.broad_link.impact: Content may be reachable by users outside the intended collaboration boundary.
sharepoint.broad_link.remediation: Reduce the sharing scope, remove stale broad links, and retest affected sites.
sharepoint.broad_link.expected_value: External and organization-wide links are absent or explicitly approved.

sharepoint.external_principal.description: SharePoint or OneDrive evidence indicates direct access for a principal outside the tenant domains.
sharepoint.external_principal.impact: Content may be exposed to external users or groups outside the approved collaboration boundary.
sharepoint.external_principal.remediation: Remove unapproved external principals from the item or site permission set and retest affected sites.
sharepoint.external_principal.expected_value: Direct SharePoint and OneDrive permissions are limited to approved tenant principals.

sharepoint.external_sharing_broad.description: SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing allows more than existing guests. Anyone links are high unless anonymous links are known to expire within 30 days and to be view-only (then medium; a setting that was not read never mitigates). New and existing guests are low: CIS 7.2.3 allows them, ScubaGear's MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1v1 does not.
sharepoint.external_sharing_broad.impact: With anyone links, anyone who obtains a link can open the content and a forwarded link cannot be tied to a person. With new guests, any user can invite an outside account that the organisation has not yet vetted.
sharepoint.external_sharing_broad.remediation: Set external sharing to existing guests or stricter (SharePoint admin center, Policies, Sharing). Where anyone links are needed, require them to expire within 30 days and limit them to view.
references: SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing settings
sharepoint.external_sharing_broad.expected_value: External sharing is limited to existing guests or the organisation; where anyone links are on, they expire within 30 days and are view-only.

sharepoint.sharing_domains_unrestricted.description: External sharing is allowed but is not limited to an allow list of approved domains. No list at all is medium (low when only existing guests may be shared with); a block list alone is low: CIS 7.2.6 accepts it, ScubaGear's MS.SHAREPOINT.1.3v1 does not.
sharepoint.sharing_domains_unrestricted.impact: Users can share with any external domain, including personal and unvetted ones, so content can reach parties the organisation has no relationship with.
sharepoint.sharing_domains_unrestricted.remediation: Limit external sharing to approved partner domains with an allow list, or block unwanted domains (SharePoint admin center, Policies, Sharing, More external sharing settings).
references: SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing settings
sharepoint.sharing_domains_unrestricted.expected_value: External sharing is limited by an allow list of approved domains, or is off.

sharepoint.default_link_type_broad.description: The default sharing link is not a link for specific people: an anyone link (high), an organisation-wide link or no default set (low). CIS 7.2.7 and ScubaGear's MS.SHAREPOINT.2.1v1 both require specific people (Direct).
sharepoint.default_link_type_broad.impact: A user who shares without changing the link type gives access to anyone holding the link, or to the whole organisation, instead of the people named.
sharepoint.default_link_type_broad.remediation: Set the default sharing link type to Specific people (Direct) in the SharePoint admin center, Policies, Sharing.
references: SharePoint and OneDrive default sharing link type
sharepoint.default_link_type_broad.expected_value: The default sharing link type is Specific people.

attack_path.app_owner_to_tier0.description: A principal that is not a tier-0 administrator owns an application or service principal that holds tier-0 rights, so it can add a credential and act with those rights.
attack_path.app_owner_to_tier0.impact: Compromising the owner gives an attacker a route to directory-wide control without ever being assigned an administrator role, and the route is not visible in role reviews.
attack_path.app_owner_to_tier0.remediation: Remove the ownership or move it to a tier-0 administrator, reduce the application's Graph permissions to what it needs, and alert on new credentials added to privileged applications.
attack_path.app_owner_to_tier0.expected_value: Only tier-0 administrators own applications that hold tier-0 rights.

attack_path.no_mfa_to_tier0.description: A user without registered MFA can reach a tier-0 role or permission through group membership, eligibility, or delegated control.
attack_path.no_mfa_to_tier0.impact: A single phished or sprayed password can be chained into directory-wide control.
attack_path.no_mfa_to_tier0.remediation: Require MFA registration for the user, remove the privileged route, and protect privileged groups and roles with phishing-resistant MFA.
attack_path.no_mfa_to_tier0.expected_value: No password-only user has a route to tier-0 control.

attack_path.privilege_escalation.description: A foothold principal (ordinary user, guest, external app, or app with a weak credential) can reach a tier-0 role or permission through a chain of memberships, role assignments, grants, or reset rights.
attack_path.privilege_escalation.impact: An attacker who compromises the foothold can escalate to tier-0 control by following the chain, often without triggering a direct role assignment.
attack_path.privilege_escalation.remediation: Break the chain at one of the listed breakpoint edges, prefer removing standing access, and review every remaining route to tier-0 roles.
attack_path.privilege_escalation.expected_value: No foothold principal has a route to tier-0 control.

app_consent.high_privilege.description: Application consent evidence shows sensitive scopes or weak ownership governance.
app_consent.high_privilege.impact: Over-privileged or unowned application consent can become a durable path to tenant data exposure.
app_consent.high_privilege.remediation: Review the consent grant, remove unused scopes, and assign accountable owners before accepting the application.
app_consent.high_privilege.expected_value: Sensitive app grants are approved, current, and owned.

app_credentials.secret_expired.description: An application credential (secret or certificate) has already expired.
app_credentials.secret_expired.impact: An expired credential indicates either an unmaintained app or a credential that should be rotated and removed; leaving expired material attached invites stale state and reuse risk.
app_credentials.secret_expired.remediation: Remove the expired credential, rotate to a fresh secret or certificate, and confirm the application is still required.
references: Microsoft Entra application credential rotation guidance
app_credentials.secret_expired.expected_value: All attached credentials are within their validity window.

app_credentials.secret_expiring.description: An application credential will expire within 30 days.
app_credentials.secret_expiring.impact: Imminent credential expiry can break automation if not rotated proactively.
app_credentials.secret_expiring.remediation: Rotate the secret or certificate, deploy the new value, and remove the soon-to-expire credential.
references: Microsoft Entra application credential rotation guidance
app_credentials.secret_expiring.expected_value: Credentials are rotated before they expire.

app_credentials.redirect_insecure.description: Application has an HTTP redirect URI pointing at a non-localhost host.
app_credentials.redirect_insecure.impact: HTTP redirect URIs can leak authorization codes and tokens to the network and bypass replay protection.
app_credentials.redirect_insecure.remediation: Replace HTTP redirect URIs with HTTPS equivalents and remove unused redirects.
app_credentials.redirect_insecure.expected_value: All non-localhost redirect URIs use HTTPS.

app_credentials.no_owner.description: Application registration has no listed owners.
app_credentials.no_owner.impact: Apps without owners drift out of governance and become hard to retire or rotate.
app_credentials.no_owner.remediation: Assign at least one accountable owner; remove the app if it is no longer required.
app_credentials.no_owner.expected_value: Each tenant-owned application has a documented owner.

app_credentials.multi_tenant_audience.description: Application sign-in audience permits multi-tenant or personal Microsoft accounts.
app_credentials.multi_tenant_audience.impact: Multi-tenant or personal-account audiences broaden the population that can interact with the app and can be misused if redirect URIs or scopes are weak.
app_credentials.multi_tenant_audience.remediation: Restrict the audience to single-tenant unless multi-tenant is explicitly required and reviewed.
app_credentials.multi_tenant_audience.expected_value: Sign-in audience is 'AzureADMyOrg' for tenant-owned apps unless multi-tenant is justified.

app_credentials.certificate_expired.description: An application certificate (keyCredential) has already expired.
app_credentials.certificate_expired.impact: Once a cert expires, downstream Microsoft and partner authentication fails; lingering expired certs also indicate weak rotation hygiene and unmaintained apps.
app_credentials.certificate_expired.remediation: Remove the expired certificate, issue a fresh one with a documented validity window, and confirm the application is still required.
references: Microsoft Entra application credential rotation guidance
app_credentials.certificate_expired.expected_value: All keyCredentials are within their validity window.

app_credentials.certificate_expiring.description: An application certificate (keyCredential) will expire within 30 days.
app_credentials.certificate_expiring.impact: Certificate rotation has more lead time than secret rotation; flagging at 30 days lets the operator schedule reissuance before authentication breaks.
app_credentials.certificate_expiring.remediation: Reissue the certificate before expiry, deploy the new value, and remove the soon-to-expire entry.
references: Microsoft Entra application credential rotation guidance
app_credentials.certificate_expiring.expected_value: keyCredentials are rotated at least 30 days before they expire.

app_credentials.secret_long_validity.description: An application secret either has no end_date_time or a validity window that exceeds two years.
app_credentials.secret_long_validity.impact: Long-lived or open-ended secrets violate cryptographic hygiene, magnify blast radius if leaked, and bypass Entra's default 24-month cap. They are a recurring root cause of supply-chain compromise.
app_credentials.secret_long_validity.remediation: Replace with a secret bounded to 6-12 months (or move to certificate auth) and rotate on a schedule.

app_credentials.credential_dormant.description: Application has not signed in for more than 365 days (signInActivity observed and null).
app_credentials.credential_dormant.impact: Stale applications expand the attack surface — credentials persist after the workload is gone, owners forget the app exists, and consent grants outlive their purpose.
app_credentials.credential_dormant.remediation: Confirm the application is still required; if not, retire it (delete, or disable and document) and revoke consent grants.
app_credentials.credential_dormant.expected_value: Application has signed in within the last year, or has been retired.

cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.description: Default cross-tenant access policy allows inbound B2B Collaboration from any external tenant.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.impact: Open inbound B2B Collaboration lets users from any external tenant be invited to resources in your tenant without per-partner scoping or trust requirements; common phishing-driven account-takeover precursor.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.remediation: Set the default B2B Collaboration inbound access to 'blocked' and enable per-partner allow-lists with inbound trust requirements (MFA, compliant device).
references: Microsoft Entra cross-tenant access default policy guidance
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.expected_value: Default inbound B2B Collaboration is 'blocked' or scoped to specific partners.

cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.description: Default cross-tenant access policy allows outbound B2B Direct Connect to any external tenant.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.impact: Open outbound Direct Connect lets your users participate in shared channels in any external tenant; sensitive content can flow out without partner-specific governance.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.remediation: Set default outbound Direct Connect to 'blocked' and enable per-partner where shared-channel collaboration is required.
references: Microsoft Entra cross-tenant access default policy guidance
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.expected_value: Default outbound B2B Direct Connect is 'blocked' or scoped per partner.

cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_in.description: Cross-tenant access policy enables automatic user consent for inbound external users.
cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_in.impact: Automatic user consent skips the per-app consent prompt for external users, removing a key data-sharing checkpoint and enabling silent over-permissioned flows.
cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_in.remediation: Disable automatic user consent inbound and require explicit user or admin consent for external app access.
references: Microsoft Entra automatic user consent settings

cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_ou.description: Cross-tenant access policy enables automatic user consent for outbound interactions with external apps.
cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_ou.impact: Outbound auto-consent lets your users grant access to data hosted in external tenants without an explicit consent prompt; weakens data-egress visibility.
cross_tenant_access.auto_user_consent_ou.remediation: Disable automatic user consent outbound; require an explicit consent step or admin approval for external app access.
references: Microsoft Entra automatic user consent settings

cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.description: Default cross-tenant access policy allows inbound B2B Direct Connect from any tenant.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.impact: Inbound B2B Direct Connect grants external identities elevated collaboration capabilities (shared channels, native Teams identity). Enabling it tenant-wide bypasses partner-specific scoping.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.remediation: Set the default B2B Direct Connect inbound access to 'blocked' and enable it explicitly per partner with inbound trust requirements (MFA, compliant device).
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_direct_c.expected_value: Default inbound B2B Direct Connect is blocked; partner-specific allow-lists are used.

cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.description: Default cross-tenant access policy permits outbound B2B Collaboration to any tenant.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.impact: Tenant users can be invited into any external tenant by default, increasing the surface for guest-account misuse and conditional access bypass.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.remediation: Restrict default outbound B2B Collaboration and approve outbound trust per partner.
cross_tenant_access.default_b2b_collabor.expected_value: Default outbound B2B Collaboration is blocked except for approved partners.

cross_tenant_access.partner_inbound_no_m.description: Partner-specific inbound B2B Direct Connect is allowed but inbound MFA trust is not accepted.
cross_tenant_access.partner_inbound_no_m.impact: Without inbound MFA trust, partner identities can authenticate with weaker controls than tenant users, undermining MFA enforcement on shared resources.
cross_tenant_access.partner_inbound_no_m.remediation: Enable inbound MFA trust acceptance for partners that allow B2B Direct Connect, or block direct connect for partners that cannot honour MFA trust.
cross_tenant_access.partner_inbound_no_m.expected_value: Partners with inbound B2B Direct Connect honour inbound MFA trust.

mailbox_forwarding.external_inbox_rule.description: An inbox rule forwards or redirects mail to a recipient outside the tenant's accepted domains.
mailbox_forwarding.external_inbox_rule.impact: External-forwarding inbox rules are the leading indicator of business email compromise (BEC) and active mailbox takeover.
mailbox_forwarding.external_inbox_rule.remediation: Disable the rule, investigate the affected mailbox for compromise, force a password reset, revoke sessions, and review sign-in logs for anomalies.
mailbox_forwarding.external_inbox_rule.expected_value: No inbox rule forwards mail to external recipients.

mailbox_forwarding.hide_from_user.description: An inbox rule moves or deletes mail in a way that hides it from the user (RSS Feeds, Junk, Deleted Items, or delete action).
mailbox_forwarding.hide_from_user.impact: Hide-from-user inbox rules are a common BEC technique to suppress visibility of fraud, replies, or forensic alerts.
mailbox_forwarding.hide_from_user.remediation: Disable the rule, audit the mailbox for compromise, and review recent inbox-rule mutations in the unified audit log.
mailbox_forwarding.hide_from_user.expected_value: Inbox rules do not silently hide messages from the user.

exchange.transport_external_redirect.description: An Exchange transport rule redirects or copies mail to a recipient outside accepted tenant domains.
exchange.transport_external_redirect.impact: Transport-level forwarding can exfiltrate many users' mail before mailbox rules or user visibility expose it.
exchange.transport_external_redirect.remediation: Remove the external recipient from the transport rule or disable the rule until the exception is approved.
exchange.transport_external_redirect.expected_value: Transport rules do not redirect or copy mail to external recipients.

exchange.remote_domain_auto_forward_enab.description: An Exchange remote-domain policy permits automatic forwarding outside the tenant.
exchange.remote_domain_auto_forward_enab.impact: Tenant-level auto-forwarding allows mailbox rules and user settings to exfiltrate mail without a transport exception.
exchange.remote_domain_auto_forward_enab.remediation: Disable automatic forwarding on the default remote-domain policy and approve only specific business exceptions.
exchange.remote_domain_auto_forward_enab.expected_value: Remote-domain policies do not allow automatic forwarding to external domains by default.

exchange.malware_filter_weakened.description: The default Exchange Online anti-malware policy has the common attachment types filter or zero-hour auto purge switched off.
exchange.malware_filter_weakened.impact: Messages with executable attachments are not filtered by type, or malware found after delivery is not removed from mailboxes, so malicious code reaches users that the policy was meant to protect.
exchange.malware_filter_weakened.remediation: Turn on the common attachment types filter and zero-hour auto purge in the default anti-malware policy, or apply the Standard or Strict preset security policy. Only the default policy is judged; custom policies and the recipients they cover are not read.
references: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 anti-malware policies
exchange.malware_filter_weakened.expected_value: The default anti-malware policy has the common attachment types filter and zero-hour auto purge on.

exchange.smtp_auth_enabled_tenant_wide.description: Authenticated SMTP client submission (SMTP AUTH) is enabled for the whole Exchange Online tenant.
exchange.smtp_auth_enabled_tenant_wide.impact: SMTP AUTH uses basic authentication, which cannot enforce MFA, so a guessed or leaked password is enough to send mail as the user.
exchange.smtp_auth_enabled_tenant_wide.remediation: Disable SMTP AUTH for the organisation (Set-TransportConfig -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $true) and enable it per mailbox only for the devices and applications that need it, ideally replaced by OAuth.
references: Microsoft Exchange Online deprecation of basic authentication for client submission
exchange.smtp_auth_enabled_tenant_wide.expected_value: SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled is true for the organisation.

exchange.dkim_signing_disabled.description: Exchange Online does not sign outbound mail with DKIM for a verified, authoritative domain.
exchange.dkim_signing_disabled.impact: Receivers cannot cryptographically authenticate mail from the domain, which weakens DMARC alignment and makes spoofing easier.
exchange.dkim_signing_disabled.remediation: Publish the selector1 and selector2 CNAME records for the domain and enable DKIM signing for it in Exchange Online. Domains with no published selector are reported by dns_posture.dkim_missing instead.
exchange.dkim_signing_disabled.expected_value: DKIM signing is enabled for every verified, authoritative domain.

dns_posture.spf_missing.description: No SPF (Sender Policy Framework) TXT record was discovered for a verified tenant domain.
dns_posture.spf_missing.impact: Without SPF, receivers cannot validate authorized senders for the domain, which raises the risk of spoofing and phishing of the tenant's brand.
dns_posture.spf_missing.remediation: Publish an SPF record at the apex (for example, 'v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all') and verify external receivers honour it.
dns_posture.spf_missing.expected_value: SPF record present with a hard-fail (-all) qualifier.

dns_posture.spf_passthrough.description: SPF record terminates with a permissive '+all' or '?all' qualifier.
dns_posture.spf_passthrough.impact: Pass-through SPF accepts mail from any sender, defeating the purpose of SPF and enabling spoofing.
dns_posture.spf_passthrough.remediation: Replace the trailing qualifier with '-all' (hard fail) or '~all' (soft fail) and revalidate.

dns_posture.dmarc_missing.description: No DMARC record was discovered at the _dmarc subdomain of a verified tenant domain.
dns_posture.dmarc_missing.impact: Without DMARC, receivers cannot enforce alignment between SPF/DKIM and the From header, leaving the domain spoofable.
dns_posture.dmarc_missing.remediation: Publish a DMARC record (start with 'v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@<domain>'), monitor reports, and progress to 'p=quarantine' or 'p=reject'.
dns_posture.dmarc_missing.expected_value: DMARC record present with an enforced policy.

dns_posture.dmarc_monitor_only.description: DMARC policy is set to 'p=none' (monitor-only) and is not enforcing alignment.
dns_posture.dmarc_monitor_only.impact: Monitor-only DMARC reports failures but does not prevent spoofed mail from being delivered.
dns_posture.dmarc_monitor_only.remediation: After validating SPF and DKIM via DMARC reports, raise the policy to 'p=quarantine' and then 'p=reject'.

dns_posture.dkim_missing.description: No DKIM selectors were discovered for a verified tenant domain.
dns_posture.dkim_missing.impact: Without DKIM, mail receivers cannot cryptographically authenticate messages, weakening DMARC alignment.
dns_posture.dkim_missing.remediation: Enable DKIM signing for the domain in Microsoft 365 (selector1/selector2) and publish the corresponding CNAME records.
dns_posture.dkim_missing.expected_value: At least one DKIM selector resolves with a valid public key.

dns_posture.spf_multiple_records.description: More than one SPF (v=spf1) TXT record is published at the domain apex.
dns_posture.spf_multiple_records.impact: RFC 7208 §4.5 mandates exactly one SPF record; multiple v=spf1 records cause receivers to return PermError, leaving the domain effectively unauthenticated.
dns_posture.spf_multiple_records.remediation: Merge SPF policy into a single record using nested 'include:' mechanisms and remove the redundant TXT entries.
dns_posture.spf_multiple_records.expected_value: Exactly one v=spf1 record at the domain apex.

dns_posture.dmarc_pct_partial.description: DMARC policy is enforcing (p=quarantine or p=reject) but only on a fraction of mail (pct<100).
dns_posture.dmarc_pct_partial.impact: Partial enforcement leaves a documented bypass: receivers apply the enforcing policy probabilistically, so spoofed mail can still be delivered to users.
dns_posture.dmarc_pct_partial.remediation: Once SPF/DKIM coverage is healthy, raise pct to 100 (or omit pct, which defaults to 100) so the policy applies to every message.

dns_posture.dmarc_rua_invalid.description: DMARC rua= aggregate-report URI list contains entries that are neither well-formed mailto: addresses nor https:// URLs.
dns_posture.dmarc_rua_invalid.impact: Invalid URIs prevent DMARC report delivery; the operator loses visibility into spoofing attempts and SPF/DKIM alignment failures.
dns_posture.dmarc_rua_invalid.remediation: Replace malformed entries with mailto:<address>@<domain> or https://<endpoint>; remove bare addresses missing the mailto: scheme and HTTP (clear-text) endpoints.
dns_posture.dmarc_rua_invalid.expected_value: All rua= URIs use mailto: with a valid address or https://.

dns_posture.bimi_logo_insecure.description: BIMI l= logo URL is not served over HTTPS.
dns_posture.bimi_logo_insecure.impact: BIMI consumers (e.g., Gmail, Yahoo) require HTTPS-served SVG logos; HTTP delivery prevents brand-indicator rendering and exposes logo fetches to tampering.
dns_posture.bimi_logo_insecure.remediation: Host the BIMI SVG over HTTPS and update the l= tag to the https:// URL.
references: BIMI draft (Brand Indicators for Message Identification)
dns_posture.bimi_logo_insecure.expected_value: BIMI l= URL uses the https:// scheme.

service_health.active_service_issue.description: An active Microsoft 365 service issue is currently affecting the tenant or one of its services.
service_health.active_service_issue.impact: Active service degradations or interruptions may invalidate evidence collected during the audit window and can mask other anomalies; operators should correlate the audit findings with the timeline of the service issue.
service_health.active_service_issue.remediation: Track the issue in the Microsoft 365 admin center service-health board, document any audit-evidence gaps caused by the outage, and re-run affected collectors once the service is restored.
service_health.active_service_issue.expected_value: No active service issues during the audit window.

external_identity.broad_guest_invite_pol.description: Authorization policy allows guest invitations from anyone (including unauthenticated members).
external_identity.broad_guest_invite_pol.impact: Tenant-wide ``allowInvitesFrom=everyone`` lets any member invite arbitrary external identities into the tenant, expanding the attack surface and bypassing partner-specific governance.
external_identity.broad_guest_invite_pol.remediation: Restrict ``allowInvitesFrom`` to ``adminsAndGuestInviters`` (CIS-recommended) or ``adminsGuestInvitersAndAllMembers`` with reviewer rotation; document who can invite externals.
external_identity.broad_guest_invite_pol.expected_value: allowInvitesFrom restricted to adminsAndGuestInviters or stricter.

consent_policy.admin_consent_workflow_di.description: Admin consent request workflow is disabled for users requiring app permissions beyond the user-consent allowlist.
consent_policy.admin_consent_workflow_di.impact: Without the admin-consent workflow, end-users either consent unilaterally to risky scopes or are blocked entirely with no escalation path — both outcomes erode tenant governance over OAuth grants.
consent_policy.admin_consent_workflow_di.remediation: Enable the admin consent request workflow (Microsoft Entra → Enterprise applications → Consent and permissions → Admin consent settings) and assign reviewers with a documented SLA.
consent_policy.admin_consent_workflow_di.expected_value: Admin consent request workflow enabled with named reviewers.

consent_policy.user_consent_unrestricted.description: The authorization policy assigns the legacy user consent policy, so any user can grant any app access to their data without administrator approval, provided the permissions do not require admin consent. Limited consent (the Microsoft-managed policy, or verified publishers and low-risk permissions) is reported by consent_policy.user_consent_limited.
consent_policy.user_consent_unrestricted.impact: Illicit consent grants let a malicious app obtain durable access to mail, files and directory data after one click by an ordinary user, with no password theft and no MFA prompt.
consent_policy.user_consent_unrestricted.remediation: In Microsoft Entra, under Enterprise applications, Consent and permissions, choose 'Do not allow user consent' and enable the admin consent workflow.
references: Microsoft Entra configure user consent settings
Microsoft Entra detect and remediate illicit consent grants

consent_policy.user_consent_limited.description: The authorization policy lets users consent to applications within limits: the Microsoft-managed policy (microsoft-user-default-recommended with its companion allow-consent-apps policy), or verified publishers with low-risk permissions (microsoft-user-default-low). CIS 5.1.5.1 asks that users cannot consent at all, and ScubaGear MS.AAD.5.2v1 fails the Microsoft-managed assignment. The permission classifications that decide which permissions count as low risk are not read, so the low-risk setting is judged conservatively.
consent_policy.user_consent_limited.impact: Users can still grant an app access to their data without administrator review, within the limits the policy sets, which a malicious or over-reaching app can stay inside.
consent_policy.user_consent_limited.remediation: In Microsoft Entra, under Enterprise applications, Consent and permissions, choose 'Do not allow user consent', enable the admin consent workflow, and review the permission grants already made.
references: Microsoft Entra configure user consent settings

consent_policy.user_consent_unverified.description: Auditex could not establish whether users can consent to applications, because the authorization policy was blocked or not collected, did not state its assigned permission grant policies, or assigns a custom or unrecognised permission grant policy whose include and exclude conditions were not evaluated.
consent_policy.user_consent_unverified.impact: The tenant's user consent control cannot be asserted from this run. The run reports neither a pass nor a failure for it.
consent_policy.user_consent_unverified.remediation: Grant the audit identity Policy.Read.All and rerun the consent_policy collector. For a custom permission grant policy, review its include and exclude conditions manually.
consent_policy.user_consent_unverified.expected_value: The authorization policy is collected and assigns only built-in permission grant policies.

identity.global_admin_singleton.description: Only one Microsoft Entra Global Administrator user was observed, counting direct, PIM-eligible and group-inherited assignments once per user. Groups and service principals are not counted.
identity.global_admin_singleton.impact: Loss or compromise of the single Global Administrator can block recovery or concentrate tenant-wide privilege.
identity.global_admin_singleton.remediation: Maintain at least two protected emergency-capable admins and use narrower roles for routine administration.
references: Microsoft Entra emergency access account guidance
identity.global_admin_singleton.expected_value: Two to four Global Administrator users (CIS 1.1.3); two to eight (CISA SCuBA MS.AAD.7.1v1).

identity.global_admin_sprawl.description: More Microsoft Entra Global Administrator users were observed than a mapped benchmark allows: CIS 1.1.3 allows two to four and CISA SCuBA MS.AAD.7.1v1 two to eight. Users are counted once whether the role is direct, PIM-eligible or inherited through a group; groups and service principals are not counted. The finding's framework_thresholds say which bound it breaches.
identity.global_admin_sprawl.impact: A broad Global Administrator set increases tenant-wide blast radius if any privileged principal is compromised.
identity.global_admin_sprawl.remediation: Reduce Global Administrator assignments and move routine administration to least-privileged roles or eligible activation.
identity.global_admin_sprawl.expected_value: Two to four Global Administrator users (CIS 1.1.3); two to eight (CISA SCuBA MS.AAD.7.1v1).

identity.global_admin_disabled.description: A disabled Microsoft Entra user still holds Global Administrator, as a direct, PIM-eligible or group-inherited assignment.
identity.global_admin_disabled.impact: Dormant privileged assignments create confusing recovery paths and can be reactivated with tenant-wide privilege.
identity.global_admin_disabled.remediation: Remove Global Administrator from disabled users and keep emergency access accounts explicitly documented.
identity.global_admin_disabled.expected_value: Disabled accounts have no Global Administrator assignments.

identity.global_admin_stale_password.description: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator, by any route (direct, PIM-eligible or through a group), has not changed password in over 365 days.
identity.global_admin_stale_password.impact: Long-lived privileged passwords raise credential-theft and recovery risk, especially for accounts without documented emergency controls.
identity.global_admin_stale_password.remediation: Rotate or validate the privileged credential and move routine administration to phishing-resistant, least-privileged access.
identity.global_admin_stale_password.expected_value: Privileged administrator credentials are rotated or governed through approved emergency-access procedure.

identity.global_admin_mfa_not_registered.description: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator, by any route (direct, PIM-eligible or through a group), has not registered an MFA method in the authentication method registration report. This reports registration only, not whether MFA is required at sign-in.
identity.global_admin_mfa_not_registered.impact: A tenant-wide privileged account with no registered MFA method cannot meet an MFA requirement and is exposed to password-only compromise.
identity.global_admin_mfa_not_registered.remediation: Register phishing-resistant MFA for every Global Administrator and confirm it in the authentication method registration report. Whether MFA is required at sign-in is assessed by the ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced rule.
identity.global_admin_mfa_not_registered.expected_value: Every Global Administrator has registered an MFA method.

identity.privileged_mfa_not_registered.description: An enabled account that holds an administrator directory role (active, PIM-eligible or inherited through a role-assignable group), or that the registration report flags as an administrator, has not registered an MFA method. Global Administrators are reported separately as critical. Guest accounts are included, because a guest administrator's MFA may be satisfied in its home tenant through cross-tenant trust; confirm that before accepting the finding. This reports registration only, not whether MFA is required at sign-in.
identity.privileged_mfa_not_registered.impact: Administrator accounts are the highest-value sign-in targets. One with no registered MFA method cannot meet an MFA requirement, so a stolen or guessed password can grant administrative control.
identity.privileged_mfa_not_registered.remediation: Register phishing-resistant MFA for the account and require MFA for administrator roles in Conditional Access. The ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced rule reports whether MFA is required of administrators at sign-in.
references: Microsoft Entra privileged access best practices
identity.privileged_mfa_not_registered.expected_value: Every account that holds an administrator role has registered an MFA method.

ca.mfa_not_enforced.description: Security defaults are off and no enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA, or an authentication strength that requires MFA, for all users on all cloud apps. Policies that are report-only, scoped to groups or roles, narrowed by platform, location, risk or device, that exclude platforms, devices or applications, or that accept a non-MFA alternative do not count. A policy that targets all users but excludes anything other than the emergency access accounts listed with --break-glass-accounts (an administrator role, a guest type, another user or group) does not require MFA of the excluded principals: the verdict is enforced_with_exclusions and this rule is raised at medium. Per-user (legacy) MFA states are not read, so this verdict does not cover a tenant that enforces MFA only through per-user MFA.
ca.mfa_not_enforced.impact: Nothing in security defaults or Conditional Access requires MFA. Unless per-user MFA is configured, which this rule does not assess, users can sign in with a password alone, so password spray, phishing and credential stuffing can succeed even where every user has registered an MFA method.
ca.mfa_not_enforced.remediation: Enable security defaults, or create an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all cloud apps and requires MFA or an MFA authentication strength. Exclude only documented emergency access accounts and list them with --break-glass-accounts, start in report-only mode, then enable. If MFA is enforced only through per-user MFA, move it to Conditional Access, which is the supported model.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: require MFA for all users
ca.mfa_not_enforced.expected_value: Security defaults are enabled, or an enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA for all users on all cloud apps and excludes only the emergency access accounts the operator listed.

ca.mfa_split_across_policies.description: Every user is required to use MFA, but only by combining policies: an enabled all-users, all-apps MFA policy excludes an administrator role (or an administrator) that a separate, role-targeted MFA policy requires MFA of. Cyber Essentials and the tenant verdict read the combined result, and this rule is not raised for it. CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations 5.2.2.2 and ScubaGear MS.AAD.3.2v1 look for one all-users policy that excludes nobody but documented emergency access accounts (ScubaGear fails any role exclusion), so they read this rule. Group and guest exclusions are not covered by a role policy and still raise ca.mfa_not_enforced.
ca.mfa_split_across_policies.impact: Protection depends on two policies staying in step: if the role policy is disabled, narrowed or loses the role, the excluded administrators are no longer required to use MFA and nothing else in the all-users policy notices.
ca.mfa_split_across_policies.remediation: Remove the role exclusion from the all-users policy and keep the role-targeted policy for the stricter requirement (for example a phishing-resistant strength), so that both apply to the administrators. Exclude only documented emergency access accounts and list them with --break-glass-accounts.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: require MFA for all users
ca.mfa_split_across_policies.expected_value: One enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA for all users on all cloud apps and excludes only the emergency access accounts the operator listed.

ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced.description: Security defaults are off and no enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA of every administrator: one that targets all users, or every directory role an administrator holds, on all cloud apps, with MFA or an MFA authentication strength, and without excluding an administrator role or an administrator. The roles come from the effective administrator set (direct, PIM-eligible and group-inherited). Policies are combined per administrator: an administrator that one policy excludes (for example an all-users policy that excludes the Global Administrator role) is covered by another enabled policy that includes the role, and a principal left out of every qualifying policy by a different route (itself in one, a group the run read in another, a role it holds in a third) counts as excluded. A policy that excludes a group or a guest type without administrator evidence reads enforced_with_exclusions and raises this rule at medium. Registration reports are not read here: they show who could use MFA, not whether it is required. Per-user (legacy) MFA states are not read.
ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced.impact: Administrator accounts are the highest-value sign-in targets. Where nothing requires them to use MFA, a stolen or guessed password grants administrative control, whether or not the administrator has registered a method.
ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced.remediation: Enable security defaults, or create an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets administrator roles, or all users, on all cloud apps and requires MFA, preferably a phishing-resistant authentication strength. Do not exclude administrator roles or administrators; exclude only documented emergency access accounts and list them with --break-glass-accounts.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: require MFA for administrators
ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced.expected_value: Security defaults are enabled, or an enabled Conditional Access policy requires MFA of every administrator role on all cloud apps with no administrator excluded.

ca.admin_mfa_role_set_incomplete.description: Administrator MFA is enforced for the administrators the tenant has today, but the enabled policies that require MFA do not, together, include every administrator role in the CIS 5.2.2.1 list (Application, Authentication, Billing, Cloud Application, Conditional Access, Exchange, Global, Helpdesk, Password, Privileged Authentication, Privileged Role, Security, SharePoint and User Administrator, and Global Reader), or exclude one of them. A role nobody holds today still counts: a policy that covers only the roles currently held, or that excludes a role nobody holds, leaves the next person given that role without an MFA requirement. A policy for all users covers every role it does not exclude. Security defaults cover every administrator role. Cyber Essentials reads the roles held today and is not affected.
ca.admin_mfa_role_set_incomplete.impact: An administrator role that no policy requires MFA for is a standing gap: the role can be assigned in a minute, and the new holder signs in with a password alone until someone notices.
ca.admin_mfa_role_set_incomplete.remediation: Target all users with the MFA policy, or add every administrator role in the CIS list to the policy's included directory roles, and remove role exclusions. Exclude only documented emergency access accounts and list them with --break-glass-accounts.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: require MFA for administrators
ca.admin_mfa_role_set_incomplete.expected_value: Enabled Conditional Access policies require MFA for all users, or for every administrator role in the CIS 5.2.2.1 list, with no administrator role excluded.

ca.admin_phishing_resistant_mfa_not_enfo.description: Administrators are required to use MFA, but no enabled Conditional Access policy requires a phishing-resistant authentication strength (the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength, or one that allows only FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business or certificate-based multi-factor credentials) of every administrator, or the phishing-resistant policies do not include every one of ScubaGear's privileged roles (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, User Administrator, SharePoint Administrator, Exchange Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, Application Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator) or exclude one of them, whoever holds it today. Security defaults require MFA of administrators but accept SMS, voice and push. This rule is raised only when administrator MFA itself is enforced; when it is not, ca.admin_mfa_not_enforced reports the larger gap.
ca.admin_phishing_resistant_mfa_not_enfo.impact: MFA by SMS, voice or push can be phished or fatigued. A phishing-resistant method removes the commonest route to taking over an administrator account.
ca.admin_phishing_resistant_mfa_not_enfo.remediation: Register FIDO2 keys or Windows Hello for Business for administrators, then require the Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength for administrator roles in Conditional Access, with an emergency access account excluded.
ca.admin_phishing_resistant_mfa_not_enfo.expected_value: Every administrator is required to use a phishing-resistant authentication method.

ca.legacy_auth_not_blocked.description: Security defaults are off and no enabled Conditional Access policy blocks the Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy client types for all users on all cloud apps. The policy must name both legacy client app types, as ScubaGear and the CIS audit require: a block of every client type (the default when client apps are not configured) does not count, and neither does a policy limited by a location condition, whether it includes only some locations or excludes any (a country block that exempts the trusted countries still allows legacy protocols from them). Policies that exclude platforms, devices or applications, or are narrowed by platform, risk or device, do not count either. A block policy that excludes anything other than the emergency access accounts listed with --break-glass-accounts leaves the excluded principals able to use legacy protocols: the verdict is blocked_with_exclusions and this rule is raised at medium. A principal that every qualifying policy leaves out by a different route (itself in one, a group the run read in another, a role it holds in a third) counts as excluded. Exchange Online protocol settings such as SMTP AUTH are not evaluated by this rule. Two block policies that each name one legacy client type (one Exchange ActiveSync, one Other) block both, but neither is the one policy the benchmarks look for: the verdict stays not_blocked with the reason legacy_block_split_across_policies and this rule is raised at medium.
ca.legacy_auth_not_blocked.impact: Legacy authentication protocols cannot perform MFA. Attackers use them for password spray and to bypass the MFA and Conditional Access requirements that apply to modern sign-in.
ca.legacy_auth_not_blocked.remediation: Create an enabled Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all cloud apps, selects the Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy client app types (and no location condition), and blocks access. Exclude only documented emergency access accounts (list them with --break-glass-accounts), start in report-only mode, then enable.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: block legacy authentication
ca.legacy_auth_not_blocked.expected_value: Security defaults are enabled, or an enabled Conditional Access policy blocks legacy authentication client types for all users on all cloud apps.

ca.enforcement_unverified.description: Auditex could not establish whether MFA is enforced (for all users or for administrators) or legacy authentication is blocked, because the Conditional Access policy list or the security defaults setting was blocked, truncated or not collected, a policy used an authentication strength that could not be checked, or the administrator set a role-targeted policy had to be compared with was not complete.
ca.enforcement_unverified.impact: The tenant's central sign-in controls cannot be asserted from this run. The run reports neither a pass nor a failure for them.
ca.enforcement_unverified.remediation: Grant the audit identity Policy.Read.All, rerun the conditional_access collector, and raise the per-endpoint limit if the policy list was truncated. The verdict evidence lists the reasons.
ca.enforcement_unverified.expected_value: Conditional Access policies and security defaults are collected completely.

identity.user_mfa_not_registered.description: A non-admin member user has not registered an MFA method in the authentication method registration report. This reports registration only, not whether MFA is required at sign-in.
identity.user_mfa_not_registered.impact: A user with no registered MFA method cannot meet an MFA requirement, so a password alone may be enough to sign in wherever MFA is not enforced.
identity.user_mfa_not_registered.remediation: Have the user register an MFA method. Check separately, with the ca.mfa_not_enforced rule, that MFA is required through Conditional Access or security defaults.
identity.user_mfa_not_registered.expected_value: Active member users have registered an MFA method.

identity.stale_enabled_account.description: An enabled account older than 90 days has no successful sign-in in the last 90 days (signInActivity observed).
identity.stale_enabled_account.impact: Unused but enabled accounts keep valid credentials, licences, and group memberships that an attacker can reuse without the owner noticing.
identity.stale_enabled_account.remediation: Confirm whether the account is still needed; disable or remove it, or document why it must stay enabled (for example a service or shared account with compensating controls). Consider an access review for inactive users.
references: Microsoft Entra manage inactive user accounts
identity.stale_enabled_account.expected_value: Enabled accounts have signed in successfully within 90 days or are disabled.

identity.privileged_stale_account.description: An enabled account holding an administrator directory role has no successful sign-in in the last 90 days (signInActivity observed).
identity.privileged_stale_account.impact: Dormant privileged accounts are high-value takeover targets: their activity is rarely watched and compromise grants administrative control of the tenant.
identity.privileged_stale_account.remediation: Remove the role assignment or disable the account if it is no longer used. Keep documented break-glass accounts monitored, and move standing admin access to eligible (PIM) assignments.
references: Microsoft Entra manage inactive user accounts
Microsoft Entra privileged access best practices
identity.privileged_stale_account.expected_value: Accounts with administrator roles are actively used or have their roles removed.

security.risky_signin.description: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs show a risky sign-in event.
security.risky_signin.impact: Risky sign-ins can indicate credential theft, impossible travel, anomalous token use, or other account-compromise signals.
security.risky_signin.remediation: Investigate the sign-in, revoke sessions where needed, reset credentials, and confirm conditional access controls responded.
security.risky_signin.expected_value: Observed sign-ins have no active risk state or elevated risk level.

security.privilege_change_event.description: Microsoft Entra directory audit logs show an administrative role or privilege change.
security.privilege_change_event.impact: Unexpected privileged-role changes can indicate persistence setup, emergency access drift, or active tenant compromise.
security.privilege_change_event.remediation: Review the initiator, target role, approval trail, and recent sign-ins; revoke unauthorized role assignments.
security.privilege_change_event.expected_value: Privileged role changes are approved, expected, and traceable.

intune.device_noncompliant.description: A managed Intune device is marked noncompliant, in conflict, or in error state.
intune.device_noncompliant.impact: Noncompliant managed devices can indicate missing security baseline enforcement or a device that should not be trusted for resource access.
intune.device_noncompliant.remediation: Review the device compliance failure, remediate or retire the device, and confirm conditional access blocks noncompliant devices where required.
intune.device_noncompliant.expected_value: Managed devices are compliant or explicitly out of scope.

intune.device_stale_sync.description: A managed Intune device has not synced within the stale-sync window (14 days by default, the Cyber Essentials window for installing updates).
intune.device_stale_sync.impact: A device that has not checked in cannot be shown to have received policy or security updates, and may be lost, retired or unmanaged.
intune.device_stale_sync.remediation: Investigate the device, retire it if it is no longer in use, and confirm Conditional Access blocks devices with unknown posture. Set the window with --stale-sync-days or AUDITEX_STALE_SYNC_DAYS.
intune.device_stale_sync.expected_value: Managed devices sync within the stale-sync window (14 days by default).

intune.device_encryption_off.description: Intune reports that a managed device's storage is not encrypted (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on macOS, device encryption on iOS and Android).
intune.device_encryption_off.impact: A lost or stolen device exposes every file on it, including cached mail and synced documents, to anyone who can read the disk.
intune.device_encryption_off.remediation: Turn on BitLocker or FileVault through an Intune endpoint security policy, require encryption in the device compliance policy, and recheck the device after its next sync. The field is read from managedDevice.isEncrypted; a device that reports no value is not flagged.
references: Microsoft Intune encrypt devices with BitLocker and FileVault
intune.device_encryption_off.expected_value: Every managed device reports isEncrypted true.

intune.device_jailbroken.description: Intune reports that a managed iOS or Android device is jailbroken or rooted.
intune.device_jailbroken.impact: A jailbroken or rooted device can run code outside the platform's security model, read app data and defeat the controls that compliance and Conditional Access rely on.
intune.device_jailbroken.remediation: Retire or reset the device, block jailbroken and rooted devices in the device compliance policy for the platform, and require compliant devices in Conditional Access. The field is read from managedDevice.jailBroken, which Intune fills for iOS and Android only.
references: Microsoft Intune device compliance settings for iOS and Android
intune.device_jailbroken.expected_value: No managed iOS or Android device reports jailBroken true.

intune.device_os_end_of_life.description: A managed device runs an operating system release whose vendor security updates have ended, according to the dated table in configs/os-end-of-life.json.
intune.device_os_end_of_life.impact: The device no longer receives security fixes, so every newly published vulnerability stays open on it. Cyber Essentials requires supported software and timely fixes.
intune.device_os_end_of_life.remediation: Upgrade the device to a supported release or replace it. Windows 10 devices enrolled in the paid Extended Security Updates programme still receive fixes, and Auditex cannot see enrolment; check the device before treating it as unpatched. Windows LTSC and IoT editions share build numbers with the General Availability releases and may remain supported; confirm the edition.
references: Microsoft Lifecycle and Windows release health
intune.device_os_end_of_life.expected_value: Every managed device runs an operating system release that still receives security updates.

intune.compliance_policy_missing_platfor.description: A platform has devices enrolled in Intune but no device compliance policy for that platform, or none of its policies is assigned.
intune.compliance_policy_missing_platfor.impact: Devices on the platform are never evaluated against a compliance baseline, so complianceState says nothing about them and Conditional Access cannot rely on it. The Intune compliance state of a device with no policy is set by the tenant's default.
intune.compliance_policy_missing_platfor.remediation: Create a device compliance policy for the platform that requires a passcode, encryption, a minimum operating system version and a jailbreak or root block, assign it to all devices or the right groups, and require compliant devices in Conditional Access. Policies built from settings-catalog templates are not listed by the endpoint Auditex reads; confirm in the Intune admin centre before acting.
intune.compliance_policy_missing_platfor.expected_value: Each platform with enrolled devices has at least one assigned device compliance policy.

intune.defender_av_off.description: Intune reports that Microsoft Defender Antivirus is not protecting a Windows device: malware protection is disabled or its service is not running.
intune.defender_av_off.impact: The device has no active anti-malware engine, so malicious code that reaches it is not blocked. Cyber Essentials requires anti-malware that is active and kept up to date.
intune.defender_av_off.remediation: Re-enable Defender Antivirus through an Intune endpoint security antivirus policy, or confirm that another anti-malware product protects the device. A device protected by a third-party product can report Defender as off; Auditex cannot see that product.
references: Microsoft Intune endpoint security antivirus policy
intune.defender_av_off.expected_value: Defender Antivirus is enabled on every Windows device, or another anti-malware product demonstrably is.

intune.defender_realtime_protection_off.description: Intune reports that Microsoft Defender real-time protection is turned off on a Windows device.
intune.defender_realtime_protection_off.impact: Files are not scanned when they are opened or written, so malware can run until the next scheduled scan.
intune.defender_realtime_protection_off.remediation: Turn real-time protection on through an Intune endpoint security antivirus policy and keep tamper protection enabled. A device protected by a third-party product can report Defender real-time protection as off.
references: Microsoft Intune endpoint security antivirus policy
intune.defender_realtime_protection_off.expected_value: Defender real-time protection is on for every Windows device protected by Defender.

intune.defender_signatures_stale.description: Intune reports that the Microsoft Defender antivirus signatures on a Windows device are out of date.
intune.defender_signatures_stale.impact: Out-of-date signatures miss recently identified malware, which weakens anti-malware protection that Cyber Essentials requires to be kept up to date.
intune.defender_signatures_stale.remediation: Check why the device cannot update its signatures (connectivity, update source, policy) and let it check in. The state is read from windowsProtectionState.signatureUpdateOverdue and productStatus.
references: Microsoft Defender Antivirus security intelligence updates
intune.defender_signatures_stale.expected_value: Defender signatures are current on every Windows device protected by Defender.

detection.unified_audit_log_disabled.description: Exchange Online reports UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled = False, so the Microsoft Purview unified audit log is not recording user and admin activity.
detection.unified_audit_log_disabled.impact: Attacker activity such as mailbox access, inbox-rule creation, file downloads, and admin changes is not recorded, and the Management Activity API and Microsoft Sentinel receive no Microsoft 365 audit data. Disabling the audit log is a known defense-evasion step (MITRE T1562.008).
detection.unified_audit_log_disabled.remediation: Turn auditing on in the Microsoft Purview portal (Audit > Start recording user and admin activity) or have an authorised admin run Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true in Exchange Online PowerShell, then confirm with Get-AdminAuditLogConfig.
detection.unified_audit_log_disabled.expected_value: UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled is True when read in Exchange Online PowerShell.

detection.mailbox_audit_disabled.description: Get-OrganizationConfig reports AuditDisabled = True, so mailbox auditing on by default is turned off for the whole organization.
detection.mailbox_audit_disabled.impact: No mailbox actions are audited, even on mailboxes whose AuditEnabled property is True. Business email compromise (MailItemsAccessed, Send, UpdateInboxRules) leaves no mailbox audit trail.
detection.mailbox_audit_disabled.remediation: Have an authorised Exchange admin run Set-OrganizationConfig -AuditDisabled $false and verify with Get-OrganizationConfig | Format-List AuditDisabled.

detection.mailbox_audit_bypass.description: One or more accounts have AuditBypassEnabled = True on their mailbox audit bypass association.
detection.mailbox_audit_bypass.impact: Every mailbox action by a bypassed account, on its own mailbox or any mailbox it can access, is not logged. A compromised bypassed account can read mail without leaving mailbox audit records.
detection.mailbox_audit_bypass.remediation: Review each bypass association with Get-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation, remove bypass for accounts that do not strictly need it (Set-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation -AuditBypassEnabled $false), and document any remaining exception.
detection.mailbox_audit_bypass.expected_value: No account has AuditBypassEnabled set to True.

detection.no_alert_policies.description: Get-ProtectionAlert returned no enabled alert policy for the tenant.
detection.no_alert_policies.impact: Suspicious activity recorded in the audit log (forwarding rules, elevation of privilege, malware campaigns) does not raise an alert, so responders learn about incidents late or not at all.
detection.no_alert_policies.remediation: Re-enable the Microsoft default alert policies in the Microsoft Defender or Purview portal and route notifications to a monitored mailbox or SIEM.
detection.no_alert_policies.expected_value: At least the default alert policies are enabled.

detection.no_risk_based_policies.description: No enabled Conditional Access policy includes signInRiskLevels or userRiskLevels conditions.
detection.no_risk_based_policies.impact: Identity Protection detections such as leaked credentials, password spray, and token anomalies do not trigger MFA, password change, or blocking automatically.
detection.no_risk_based_policies.remediation: If the tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P2, create Conditional Access policies that require MFA for medium or high sign-in risk and a secure password change for high user risk, start in report-only mode, then enable.
detection.no_risk_based_policies.expected_value: At least one enabled Conditional Access policy acts on sign-in or user risk.

detection.signin_logs_unavailable.description: Microsoft Graph refused /auditLogs/signIns with a licensing error, so Entra sign-in logs are not available to the audit identity or to downstream tooling.
detection.signin_logs_unavailable.impact: Without sign-in logs, investigators cannot trace password spray, token theft, risky locations, or legacy-authentication use, and those events cannot be exported to a SIEM.
detection.signin_logs_unavailable.remediation: License the tenant for Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher so sign-in logs are retained and readable through Microsoft Graph, then rerun the security collector.
detection.signin_logs_unavailable.expected_value: Sign-in logs are readable through Microsoft Graph.

dns_posture.mta_sts_missing.description: No MTA-STS TXT record (v=STSv1) was found at _mta-sts.<domain> for a verified custom domain.
dns_posture.mta_sts_missing.impact: Sending servers cannot require TLS or validate the receiving certificate for this domain, so inbound mail can be downgraded or intercepted in transit.
dns_posture.mta_sts_missing.remediation: Host an MTA-STS policy at https://mta-sts.<domain>/.well-known/mta-sts.txt, publish the _mta-sts TXT record, start in testing mode, then move to enforce.
dns_posture.mta_sts_missing.expected_value: MTA-STS TXT record and policy published in enforce mode.

dns_posture.mta_sts_testing_mode.description: The domain publishes an MTA-STS policy whose mode is testing or none.
dns_posture.mta_sts_testing_mode.impact: Senders report TLS failures but still deliver over unprotected connections, so the policy does not stop downgrade or interception.
dns_posture.mta_sts_testing_mode.remediation: After TLS reports show no failures, change the policy mode to enforce and update the id value in the _mta-sts TXT record.

dns_posture.mta_sts_policy_invalid.description: The _mta-sts TXT record exists, but https://mta-sts.<domain>/.well-known/mta-sts.txt could not be fetched or did not contain a valid STSv1 policy.
dns_posture.mta_sts_policy_invalid.impact: Senders that honour MTA-STS cannot obtain a valid policy, which can cause delivery failures once a cached policy expires and leaves the domain without the intended transport protection.
dns_posture.mta_sts_policy_invalid.remediation: Serve a valid STSv1 policy over HTTPS with a certificate for mta-sts.<domain>, without redirects, and update the TXT record id after each change.
dns_posture.mta_sts_policy_invalid.expected_value: MTA-STS policy file returns HTTP 200 with a valid STSv1 policy.

dns_posture.tls_rpt_missing.description: No SMTP TLS Reporting record (v=TLSRPTv1) was found at _smtp._tls.<domain>.
dns_posture.tls_rpt_missing.impact: The domain owner receives no reports about failed or downgraded TLS sessions, so interception attempts and MTA-STS misconfiguration go unnoticed.
dns_posture.tls_rpt_missing.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _smtp._tls.<domain> such as 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls-reports@<domain>' and monitor the reports.
dns_posture.tls_rpt_missing.expected_value: TLS-RPT record published with a monitored reporting address.

exposure.federated_domain_metadata_publi.description: A verified domain is federated, and the tenant's public OpenID discovery metadata for the domain is readable without credentials. Anyone can learn the tenant ID and that sign-in is handed to an external identity provider.
exposure.federated_domain_metadata_publi.impact: Informational. The public footprint helps attackers target the federation provider (for example forged SAML tokens against a compromised IdP). It is not a misconfiguration by itself.
exposure.federated_domain_metadata_publi.remediation: No change is needed for the metadata itself. Keep the federation provider patched and monitored, protect its token-signing keys, and consider moving the domain to managed (cloud) authentication.
exposure.federated_domain_metadata_publi.expected_value: Federated domains are known, documented, and their identity provider is monitored.

secure_score.low_overall.title: Microsoft Secure Score is below half of the achievable score
secure_score.low_overall.description: The latest Microsoft Secure Score snapshot returned by Microsoft Graph is below 50% of the maximum achievable score.
secure_score.low_overall.impact: Microsoft's own posture assessment reports that more than half of the available security controls are not implemented, so baseline gaps are likely across identity, email, and data protection.
secure_score.low_overall.remediation: Review the Secure Score reconciliation table in the report pack, confirm the gaps that Auditex findings also show, and plan improvement actions for the highest-weight controls first.
secure_score.low_overall.expected_value: Secure Score current score is at least 50% of the maximum score.

sharepoint.site_orphaned.description: A SharePoint site shows no principal in its sampled permissions, so nobody is accountable for who can reach its content.
sharepoint.site_orphaned.impact: An orphaned site keeps its permissions and sharing links while no owner reviews them, so stale and external access persists unnoticed.
sharepoint.site_orphaned.remediation: Assign at least two active owners to the site or retire it, then review its members and sharing links.
sharepoint.site_orphaned.expected_value: Every SharePoint site has at least two active owners.

sharepoint.site_weak_ownership.description: A SharePoint site shows a single principal in its sampled permissions, so one account change leaves the site without an owner.
sharepoint.site_weak_ownership.impact: A site that depends on one owner is likely to become orphaned, and its access then goes unreviewed.
sharepoint.site_weak_ownership.remediation: Assign at least two active owners to the site and confirm each one still needs it.
sharepoint.site_weak_ownership.expected_value: Every SharePoint site has at least two active owners.

onedrive.external_sharing_enabled.description: OneDrive is set to allow sharing outside the organisation. This is one finding for the tenant, not one per site: anyone links are rated high, new and existing guests low, and the personal sites the setting covers are listed in the evidence.
onedrive.external_sharing_enabled.impact: Users can share work files outside the organisation without review, which exposes content beyond the approved collaboration boundary. Anyone links also cannot be tied to a person.
onedrive.external_sharing_enabled.remediation: Limit OneDrive sharing to existing guests or to the organisation, or to named partner domains, and review existing external shares.
onedrive.external_sharing_enabled.expected_value: OneDrive sharing is limited to existing guests or the organisation, with anyone links off.

exchange.mailbox_forwarding_configured.description: A mailbox forwards mail to an SMTP address (ForwardingSmtpAddress) or to a mail contact or mailbox (ForwardingAddress) configured on the mailbox itself.
exchange.mailbox_forwarding_configured.impact: Mailbox-level forwarding copies mail out of the tenant without a transport rule, and it is a common persistence step after a mailbox takeover.
exchange.mailbox_forwarding_configured.remediation: Remove the forwarding address or contact unless an approved business case exists, and confirm the mailbox was not compromised.
exchange.mailbox_forwarding_configured.expected_value: No mailbox has a forwarding SMTP address or forwarding contact unless it is approved.

teams.external_federation_open.description: Microsoft Teams federation is allowed with no allow list of partner domains, so users in every external organisation can contact staff directly. Federation limited to an allow list is not reported.
teams.external_federation_open.impact: Open federation lets outside parties contact staff directly, which supports phishing and data sharing outside approved partners. A block list removes named domains only; it does not make federation selective.
teams.external_federation_open.remediation: Limit external access to an allow list of partner domains in the Teams admin center (External access), or turn it off where it is not needed.
teams.external_federation_open.expected_value: Teams external access is limited to an allow list of approved partner domains, or is off.

identity_governance.standing_privilege_o.description: Privileged role assignments exist without any eligibility schedules, so privileged access is permanent rather than time-bound.
identity_governance.standing_privilege_o.impact: Standing privilege widens the window in which a stolen administrator credential can be used.
identity_governance.standing_privilege_o.remediation: Move administrator roles to eligible assignments in Privileged Identity Management and activate them only when needed.
identity_governance.standing_privilege_o.expected_value: Privileged roles are eligible and time-bound, with standing assignments limited to emergency access accounts.

intune_depth.policies_without_assignment.description: Intune device configuration profiles were read in full (every profile's assignments included) and none of them has an assignment. Compliance policies, app protection policies and Conditional Access policies are not counted.
intune_depth.policies_without_assignment.impact: A policy that is assigned to nobody enforces nothing, so devices may be unmanaged although a baseline appears to exist.
intune_depth.policies_without_assignment.remediation: Assign each Intune policy to the intended device or user groups and confirm devices receive it.
intune_depth.policies_without_assignment.expected_value: Every in-scope Intune policy is assigned to a device or user group.

intune_depth.update_ring_not_assigned.description: Windows devices are enrolled in Intune but no Windows Update for Business update ring is assigned to any group, all devices or all users, and no assigned Windows update profile or Configuration Manager co-managed device was seen.
intune_depth.update_ring_not_assigned.impact: Intune does not control how and when Windows quality updates install through an update ring, so update behaviour depends on each device's local defaults and Cyber Essentials patching cannot be evidenced from the tenant.
intune_depth.update_ring_not_assigned.remediation: Create a Windows Update for Business update ring with a quality update deferral of 14 days or less and a deadline, and assign it to all Windows devices. A ring assigned only to groups is not flagged, because Auditex does not resolve group membership. Update settings made through settings catalog policies, group policy, Configuration Manager or WSUS are not read: a tenant that manages updates only that way should confirm in the Intune admin centre before acting. An assigned update profile or a co-managed Windows device makes the rule not assessed instead of failed.
references: Microsoft Intune Windows 10 and later update rings
intune_depth.update_ring_not_assigned.expected_value: At least one Windows Update for Business update ring is assigned and covers the Windows devices.

intune_depth.update_ring_deferral_excess.description: An assigned Windows Update for Business update ring lets quality updates wait more than 14 days: the deferral alone exceeds 14 days, or the deferral plus the deadline and restart grace period does, or quality updates are paused.
intune_depth.update_ring_deferral_excess.impact: Security fixes install later than the 14 days Cyber Essentials allows for critical and high-risk updates, so devices on this ring stay exposed longer than the standard permits.
intune_depth.update_ring_deferral_excess.remediation: Reduce the quality update deferral so that deferral, deadline and restart grace period add up to 14 days or less, resume paused updates, and use a deadline to force installation. The ring's settings are read from windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration.
references: Microsoft Intune Windows 10 and later update rings
Cyber Essentials Requirements for IT Infrastructure, security update management
intune_depth.update_ring_deferral_excess.expected_value: Assigned update rings defer quality updates by 14 days or less and are not paused.

ca.policy_report_only.description: A Conditional Access policy is in report-only mode, so it records its decision but does not enforce it.
ca.policy_report_only.impact: Users and devices the policy was meant to control are not held to it, although the tenant appears to have the policy.
ca.policy_report_only.remediation: Review the report-only results, then enable the policy or retire it.
references: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access report-only mode
ca.policy_report_only.expected_value: Conditional Access policies are enabled, or report-only for a documented and short evaluation period.

ca.break_glass_exclusion_missing.description: One or more enabled Conditional Access policies that require MFA, require a compliant or hybrid-joined device with no MFA alternative, or block sign-ins exclude none of the emergency-access accounts. The accounts are the ones the operator listed, or, without a list, accounts inferred from names and the Global Administrator role. The finding names each policy. Report-only policies and policies without an MFA, device or block grant are not judged.
ca.break_glass_exclusion_missing.impact: A policy or sign-in service failure can lock out every administrator, including the accounts kept for recovery.
ca.break_glass_exclusion_missing.remediation: Exclude the emergency-access accounts (or the group that holds them) from the named policies, protect them with a phishing-resistant method, and monitor their sign-ins separately. List the accounts with --break-glass-accounts or AUDITEX_BREAK_GLASS_ACCOUNTS so the check does not rely on inference.
ca.break_glass_exclusion_missing.expected_value: Emergency-access accounts are excluded from every enabled policy that requires MFA or a managed device, or blocks sign-ins, and are monitored.

identity.admin_set_unverified.description: Auditex could not establish who holds an administrator role, because the role definitions, the role assignments, the PIM schedules or the membership fan-out of role-assignable groups was blocked, truncated or not collected.
identity.admin_set_unverified.impact: The Global Administrator count and the checks on each administrator rest on part of the set. The run reports neither a pass nor a failure for the count rules; an administrator reached only through a source that was not read can be missing from every administrator check.
